answer: One workable design: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because horizon only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, opal is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any vine approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
